Figure 2.2 shows the histogram ofbirthwgt_oz, which is the ounces part of
birth weight. In theory we expect this distribution to beuniform; that is, all
values should have the same frequency. In fact, 0 is more common than the
other values, and 1 and 15 are less common, probably because respondents
round off birth weights that are close to an integer value.

Figure 2.3 shows the histogram ofagepreg, the mother’s age at the end of
pregnancy. The mode is 21 years. The distribution is very roughly bellshaped, but in this case the tail extends farther to the right than left; most
mothers are in their 20s, fewer in their 30s.
